subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible requests ignore or tolerate a generic OpenAI body `model`, and should that rule apply beyond `/v1/chat/completions`?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but it changes the public model-selection contract and may need parity across Responses and embeddings rather than a one-endpoint workaround.

options.title: Adopt header precedence consistently
options.body: A valid agent header selects the agent, generic body models are treated as client compatibility metadata, and docs/tests are updated across the chosen OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

options.title: Preserve the agent-first body contract
options.body: Clients must continue sending `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>` in `model`, with `x-openclaw-model` reserved for backend provider/model overrides.

options.title: Add a chat-only exception
options.body: Only `/v1/chat/completions` tolerates generic body models with a valid agent header, accepting the risk of endpoint-specific semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt header precedence consistently
recommendation.body: A valid agent header selects the agent, generic body models are treated as client compatibility metadata, and docs/tests are updated across the chosen OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the agent-first contract and the related OpenAI-compatible endpoint expansion, making them the strongest history-based owner for the API precedence choice.
